newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end at 5-1/2 year low.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end at 5-1/2 year low.

text.p: Thai stocks tumbled 2.55 percent on Tuesday, pushing the market index down to its lowest finish since November 1, 1991.

Lingering market concerns over the sluggish Thai economy and weak corporate earnings forced the SET Index to retreat 16.82 points to 643.28. The SET 50 fell 1.37 points, or 2.81 percent, to close at its all-time low of 47.35 on moderate 3.02 billion baht turnover.
The sharp decline was mainly brought by jitters over the slowing economy's short and medium-term prospects, traders said.
They said slowing economic growth this year, forecast at a decade low of five percent, and few clear signs that the economic downturn is about to bottom out sparked sales across the board.

The finance sector, beset by worries of weak loan quality, investment portfolio losses and low broking revenues, lost 4.54 percent. Property stocks shed 4.46 percent and the communications counter fell 5.13 percent.
"Everything outside Thailand looks good at the moment, but here sentiment looks pretty bearish and the simple answer is the economy," said a trader at a Thai Farmers Bank affiliate.

Communications stocks suffered after some foreign research houses downgraded the sector which, they said, was partly hurt by its increasing liberalisation that threatens mobile phone operators, traders said.
"Some foreign houses have underweighed the telecoms sector because of liberalisation in the mobile phone sector," said a local trader.
Among key losers was Advanced Info Services which lost 15 baht to 160.
Among heavily traded stocks was Bangkok Bank of Commerce which ended its rally last week by falling 0.80 baht to 8.10.
Retail discount store operator Siam Makro shed 4.50 baht to 52.00, and Land and House dropped seven baht to 65.00.
